economics.objectives-define2.0001.all: Firm aims to produce output where TR minus TC is greatest (MC=MR), earning the largest possible profit.

economics.objectives-describe.0015.all: New/struggling firm or recession: priority is covering costs to stay in business, since a firm that closes cannot earn any profit later.

economics.objectives-evaluate-1.0001.all: Plan: For - excess demand (classes full), more revenue, economies of scale, spread risk. Against - costs/risk of new premises, demand may not exist in other area, management stretched, quality loss. Judgement depends on demand evidence and finance.

economics.objectives-evaluate-2.0001.all: Plan: Benefits - economies of scale may lower prices, more investment/innovation. Costs - 47% share gives market power, higher prices, less choice, less incentive to be efficient. Depends on regulator, remaining competition, whether savings passed on.

economics.objectives-evaluate-3.0002.all: Plan: Profit max - rewards owners, funds investment. Market share/sustainability - long-run growth, brand, consumer loyalty, may sacrifice short-run profit. Principal-agent conflict; judgement: long-run profit may be served by sustainability.

economics.objectives-explain.0003.all: Manager may aim for sales/market share growth (or own bonus tied to sales); discount attracts bulk buyers, raising sales volume and market share though lowering profit margin per unit.

economics.objectives-mcq-class.0014.all: To benefit from economies of scale

economics.objectives-mcq-def.0002.all: When a firm grows internally by increasing output, for example opening new branches

economics.objectives-state-class.0001.all: Owner wants to keep control (or small/local market, personal service)

economics.ped-analyse-1.0004.all: Monopoly and commuters rely on buses -> inelastic -> %fall in Qd < 18%, TR rises. But trains/bike hire are substitutes -> demand on those routes more elastic -> larger fall in Qd, TR may fall. Net effect depends on overall PED.

economics.ped-analyse-2.0005.all: PED -0.3: Qd falls about 5.4% for 18% price rise; consumers pay more, spend more of income on cigarettes, reduced real income esp. poor (regressive); some quit/cut down, health gains; possible black market.

economics.ped-analyse-3.0001.all: Premium brand elastic (many substitutes): cut price raises TR. Basic habit product inelastic: raise price raises TR. Knowing PED lets firm set different strategies for each product.

economics.ped-assess-1.0006.all: Plan: inelastic for commuters/monopoly -> TR rises; substitutes on some routes -> elastic -> TR falls; long-run elasticity higher; judgement depends on proportion of routes with alternatives.

economics.ped-assess-2.0006.all: Plan: PED -0.3 inelastic -> Qd falls ~4.5%, so revenue rises (aim 1 met) but consumption reduction small (aim 2 weakly met); conflict between aims; smuggling, long-run elasticity higher.

economics.ped-assess-3.0005.all: Plan: cut premium (elastic) price -> TR rises; cut basic (inelastic) price -> TR falls; so no, only cut premium; caveats: competitor reaction, PED estimates uncertain, costs.

economics.ped-data.0002.b: Commuters reliant + monopoly -> inelastic -> TR rises; substitutes (trains, bikes) on some routes -> more elastic -> TR may fall.
economics.ped-data.0002.c: Plan: inelastic overall -> TR rises; elastic on routes with substitutes; long run more elastic; depends on proportion of passengers with alternatives; overall likely TR rises short run.

economics.ped-define1.0003.all: When % change in quantity demanded is smaller than the % change in price (PED between 0 and -1).

economics.ped-define2.0006.all: Total money received from selling output; price x quantity sold.

economics.ped-describe.0010.all: With elastic demand, price and TR move in opposite directions: a price rise lowers TR and a price cut raises TR, because %dQd > %dP.

economics.ped-diagram.0001.all: Draw a shallow (flat) downward-sloping demand curve; mark P1 and P2 (higher) on price axis, Q1 and Q2 on quantity axis, showing large fall in Qd from Q1 to Q2 (proportionately larger than price rise).

economics.ped-evaluate-1.0005.all: Plan: monopoly, commuters -> inelastic -> TR rises; substitutes trains/bikes -> elastic on some routes -> TR falls; long run, income, size of rise; judgement depends on PED value.

economics.ped-evaluate-2.0001.all: Plan: PED -0.4 -> Qd falls ~12% for 30% price rise -> revenue rises; consumption falls modestly; conflict between aims; substitutes, long-run elasticity, regressive, alternative policies (education, regulation).

economics.ped-evaluate-3.0004.all: Plan: premium elastic -> price cut raises TR; basic inelastic -> price cut lowers TR; recommend cutting only premium; caveats: price war, costs/profit, PED estimates.

economics.ped-explain.0009.all: PED -0.5 is inelastic, so quantity falls only slightly when tax raises price; government raises substantial tax revenue (or: to reduce consumption of a demerit good with negative externalities).

economics.objectives-state-class.0001.problem: Grammatical error in stem: 'a firm may stays small'.
economics.objectives-state-class.0001.fix: State one reason why a firm may stay small.

economics.ped-data.0002.problem: Part (a) asks about smartphones priced EUR8 to EUR9 sold by a bus operator, which contradicts Extract A (bus fares) and is implausible.
economics.ped-data.0002.fix: Reword (a) to bus fares, e.g. 'Northgate Holdings changed a single fare from EUR8 to EUR9; weekly passengers fell from 810 to 460' (answer -3.46 unchanged).
